text:
Maya: quick heads-up, ran a regional kernel sweep for gpt-v1.2 (seq=1024) — flashv2 / flashv3 / triton, H100 vs A100, q8 quant. posting highlights below.
Maya: command used:
```
./bench --model gpt-v1.2 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --quant q8 --kernels flashv3,flashv2,triton --gpus H100,A100 --regions us-east,eu-west,apac --samples 500 --out gs://redwood-bench/1991234567/
```
bench-bot: upload complete: gs://redwood-bench/1991234567/metrics.csv (also perf tarball) :rocket:
Samir: nice. first pass — any obvious regressions?
Maya: yes — flashv3 wins p99 latency on H100 in us-east and eu-west (~12% lower than flashv2), but in APAC on H100 L40 we saw p50/p95 bump and tail jitter; throughput also dropped ~8% vs flashv2 for long seqs.
Oliver: interesting — is that consistent across runs or noisy microburst?
Maya: fairly consistent across 5 repeats. CPU-side logs show more CPU stalls during block allocation on apac workers. stack traces point to kernel launch overlap differences.
Anya: did you check triton vendor kernels on APAC? sometimes they win tail.
Maya: triton had smoother tail on A100 in apac for q8, but lower raw throughput (~6% vs flashv2). On H100 triton lagged.
Samir: how about quality delta from quant? any generation regressions after q8 quantization?
Maya: eval suite (200 prompts) shows +0.3 ppl and 0.6% exact-match drop — small overall. but a tiny cluster of prompts with long-range math completions had hallucinations more often with q8.
Anya: we should flag those prompt patterns in quality monitor before switching kernels for customer traffic.
Oliver: proposal: switch heuristic that combines latency and quality signals, not just latency. e.g. trigger kernel switchover when both: (a) relative p99 latency > +7% AND (b) throughput drop > 10% OR model-quality delta > 1% on the alertset.
Samir: add hysteresis: require condition hold for 3 consecutive 5m windows to avoid flapping.
Maya: agreed. also add regional weighting — if apac only, prefer vendor/triton on H100 L40 until kernel provider ships patch.
bench-bot: summary metrics (abbrev):
- us-east H100 flashv3: p50 38ms, p95 82ms, p99 130ms, throughput 950 tok/s
- eu-west H100 flashv3: p50 41ms, p95 85ms, p99 135ms, throughput 930 tok/s
- apac H100 flashv3: p50 62ms, p95 140ms, p99 260ms, throughput 880 tok/s
- apac H100 flashv2: p50 58ms, p95 120ms, p99 200ms, throughput 950 tok/s
- apac A100 triton (q8): p50 70ms, p95 125ms, p99 210ms, throughput 880 tok/s
Maya: file with full CSV + logs: gs://redwood-bench/1991234567/metrics.csv
Oliver: can you capture kernel vendor versions and driver/kernel mismatches in the artifact? those often explain apac differences.
Maya: done — uploaded runtime_manifest.json and nv_driver.txt. apac nodes are on nvidia-driver 535.43, us/eu are 535.67.
Samir: driver mismatch could be the smoking gun. we should repro APAC using same driver as us-east before policy changes.
Anya: for rollout plan: 1) repro on apac with driver parity, 2) run quality evals on the flagged prompt set, 3) if repro persists, enable traffic canary: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback to flashv2 if p99 > +10% or quality delta > 1.5%.
Maya: I'll kick off driver-parity repro and schedule a 1h bench slot tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
Oliver: also add metric for token-emission stalls (we saw those in logs) and bind alarm to it.
bench-bot: action items created: PERF-778 (repro apac with driver parity), PERF-779 (add kernel hysteresis rules), PERF-780 (add flagged prompts to quality monitor).
Samir: thanks Maya — big help. ping us when repro is done. :thumbsup:
Maya: will do.
Anya: adding a note — when we switch kernels automatically, ensure model-version pin is respected (don't cross-roll model+kernel in same canary).
Oliver: agreed. last thing: let's capture a small microbenchmark with seq=2048 and batch=1 to amplify tail behavior for kernel maintainers.
Maya: adding that to the repro job.
bench-bot: repro job scheduled: 1991234567-repro-01 (03:00 UTC).
